title: Passenger Planes Nearly Collide Far More Than You Know

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空度过的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 上千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用一个不同的首字母单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我很喜欢一锅端的食谱，因为我讨厌洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》致力于陪伴您理解世界并充分利用每一天，今年迎来175周年。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nytimes.com/subscribe上的特惠。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barrow.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴罗，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, a Times investigation has found that U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天，《时报》的一项调查发现，美国

sentences.en: passenger planes come dangerously close to crashing into each other far more frequently than the public knows.
sentences.zh: 客机发生险情、差点相撞的频率，远比公众知道的要高得多。

sentences.en: My colleague, Sydney Ember, explains why an aviation system known for its safety is producing such a steady stream of close calls.
sentences.zh: 我的同事悉尼·埃姆伯将向我们解释，为什么以安全性闻名的航空系统会频频出现险情。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, September 5th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月5日，星期二。

sentences.en: Sydney, tell us how this investigation started for you.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，跟我们讲讲这项调查是怎么开始的吧。

sentences.en: So you might remember back in the winter, travel for passengers became a total nightmare.
sentences.zh: 大家可能还记得，在冬天的时侯，旅客出行简直成了一场噩梦。

sentences.en: Southwest had a meltdown, and then a couple weeks later, there was a system failure at the Federal
sentences.zh: 西南航空发生了系统瘫痪，紧接着几周后，联邦

sentences.en: Aviation Administration.
sentences.zh: 航空管理局也出现了系统故障。

sentences.en: And this led to lots of delays, lots of cancellations, and thousands of passengers were stranded.
sentences.zh: 这导致了大量的航班延误、取消，成千上万的旅客滞留。

sentences.en: They were livid.
sentences.zh: 他们气急败坏。

sentences.en: Congress was mad.
sentences.zh: 国会也大发雷霆。

sentences.en: And our editor came to us and essentially said, go figure out why air travel is so annoying.
sentences.zh: 我们的编辑找到我们，基本上就是说，去弄清楚为什么航空旅行这么令人恼火。

sentences.en: Right, and seemingly so broken.
sentences.zh: 没错，而且看起来问题重重。

sentences.en: And seemingly so broken.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来问题重重。

sentences.en: And so we started talking to people in the aviation industry.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始和航空业的人交谈。

sentences.en: We started talking to people who worked at airlines, pilots.
sentences.zh: 我们开始和航空公司的工作人员、飞行员交谈。

sentences.en: We started talking to air traffic controllers, really anyone we could think of who might be able to explain this to us.
sentences.zh: 我们开始和空中交通管制员交谈，真的任何我们能想到能向我们解释这一点的人。

sentences.en: And what they started saying was, actually, there is a more important story here to tell, and it's about safety.
sentences.zh: 而他们开始说的是，其实这里有一个更重要、更值得讲述的故事，那就是关于安全的。

sentences.en: The safety system underlying, aviation underlying safety for planes and passengers is under tremendous stress.
sentences.zh: 飞机和乘客安全背后的航空安全系统正承受着巨大的压力。

sentences.en: And at the same time, we started seeing a spate of public near misses.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们开始看到一连串公开报道的差点相撞事件。

sentences.en: And these were near collisions between two planes that were occurring generally around or at airports.
sentences.zh: 这些都是两架飞机在机场附近或机场发生的差点相撞事件。

sentences.en: A terrifying near miss between two passenger planes on the runway at New York's JFK airport.
sentences.zh: 在纽约肯尼迪机场的跑道上，两架客机发生了一起极其惊险的差点相撞事件。

sentences.en: There was one incident in mid-January at JFK.
sentences.zh: 1月中旬在肯尼迪机场发生了一起事故。

sentences.en: Delta 1943 canceled takeoff plans.
sentences.zh: 达美1943航班取消了起飞计划。

sentences.en: An American Airlines plane made a wrong turn and crossed a runway as a Delta plane was taking off.
sentences.zh: 一架美国航空公司的飞机拐错了方向，在达美航空飞机起飞时穿过了跑道。

sentences.en: You could feel a jolt as the brakes activated.
sentences.zh: 当刹车启动时，你能感觉到一阵猛烈的晃动。

sentences.en: Several weeks later.
sentences.zh: 几周后。

sentences.en: In Austin, an airport crisis caught just in time.
sentences.zh: 在奥斯汀，一场机场危机被及时化解。

sentences.en: A FedEx plane was cleared to land as a Southwest plane was cleared to take off.
sentences.zh: 一架联邦快递的飞机获准降落，而一架西南航空的飞机获准起飞。

sentences.en: Just seconds away from disaster, the FedEx pilots initiated what is called a go-around.
sentences.zh: 离灾难只有几秒钟之遥，联邦快递的飞行员启动了所谓的复飞程序。

sentences.en: There were other incidents in Sarasota, one in Boston.
sentences.zh: 在萨拉索塔和波士顿还发生了其他事故。

sentences.en: It was just the latest instance of a close call at an airport, leaving many wondering, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 这只是机场频频出现险情的最新例证，让许多人不禁疑惑：到底怎么了？

sentences.en: It was just a whole slew of incidents that directed attention on whether aviation, you know, flying, as we know it, is safe.
sentences.zh: 这一连串的事故让人把注意力集中在航空业，也就是我们所知的飞行是否安全上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it sounds like just as people in the industry are telling you, hey, there's a safety problem,
sentences.zh: 所以听起来，正如业内人士对你所说的那样，嘿，这里有个安全问题，

sentences.en: focus on that, that you can't not focus on it because these incidents are starting to happen.
sentences.zh: 关注它吧，你不能不关注，因为这些事故开始发生了。

sentences.en: So what did you do next?
sentences.zh: 那你接下来做了什么？

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: We continue to talk to people and we started asking them, are these incidents that have been occurring across the country?
sentences.zh: 我们继续与人们交谈，并开始询问他们，全国各地发生的这些事故，

sentences.en: Are there more of them than we know about?
sentences.zh: 是不是比我们知道的还要多？

sentences.en: And also what's causing them?
sentences.zh: 以及是什么导致了这些事故？

sentences.en: And what they told us was there is no real authoritative, comprehensive source that shows how many commercial planes are coming into these near collisions.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们，并没有一个真正权威、全面的来源来显示有多少商业客机险些相撞。

sentences.en: And so what I started doing with my colleague, Emily Steele, was digging around and trying to
sentences.zh: 因此，我和我的同事艾米丽·斯蒂尔开始四处挖掘，试图

sentences.en: figure out if we could identify close calls that hadn't been publicly reported or that most of the public wouldn't know about.
sentences.zh: 弄清楚我们能否查明那些未被公开报道或大多数公众并不知情的险情。

sentences.en: So we started combing through public databases, including one maintained by NASA that have reports by pilots, air traffic controllers, really anyone involved in aviation about any
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始梳理公共数据库，其中包括由美国宇航局维护的一个数据库，里面有飞行员、空中交通管制员，以及真正参与航空事务的任何人关于任何

sentences.en: safety issues, including close calls.
sentences.zh: 安全问题（包括险情）的报告。

sentences.en: And eventually we were also able to gain access to these safety reports that detail incidents
sentences.zh: 最终，我们还得以查阅这些详细记录全国各地事故的安全报告，

sentences.en: across the country that are distributed to a select group of employees at the Federal Aviation
sentences.zh: 这些报告仅分发给联邦航空管理局的一小部分精选员工。

sentences.en: Administration.
sentences.zh: 管理局。

sentences.en: And so putting all of this together, these safety reports, these public databases, a picture
sentences.zh: 因此，把所有这些放在一起——这些安全报告、这些公共数据库，一幅画面

sentences.en: started to emerge of a lot more close calls than almost anyone realizes are happening, occurring extremely frequently, really alarmingly frequently.
sentences.zh: 开始浮现：差点相撞的次数比几乎任何人意识到的都要多得多，发生得极其频繁，真的达到令人堪忧的频繁程度。

sentences.en: Well, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Just how frequently, just how alarmingly frequently did you find based on all this data that these close calls are happening?
sentences.zh: 根据所有这些数据，你发现这些险情发生的频率到底有多高，究竟达到了怎样令人堪忧的频繁程度？

sentences.en: So, using these safety reports and these other databases, what we found was this was happening multiple times on average every week.
sentences.zh: 所以，通过这些安全报告和其他数据库，我们发现平均每周都会多次发生这种情况。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And we looked at July, for example, and we saw at least 46 close calls that had occurred involving commercial passenger planes in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 比如我们看了7月份的数据，发现在美国涉及商业客机的差点相撞事件至少有46起。

sentences.en: Wait, I just want to pause on that.
sentences.zh: 等等，我只想在这停顿一下。

sentences.en: That means more than once a day, 46 times in a single month.
sentences.zh: 这意味着平均一天不止一次，一个月内发生了46次。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: On average, it seemed like they were happening more than once a day.
sentences.zh: 平均下来，它们发生的频率似乎超过了一天一次。

sentences.en: And then when we looked at the NASA database, for the most recent 12-month period for which data is available, what we saw was roughly 300 documented reports of close calls on the
sentences.zh: 然后当我们查看美国宇航局的数据库时，在有数据可查的最近12个月期间，我们看到大约有300起有据可查的地面和空中险情报告。

sentences.en: ground and in the air.
sentences.zh: 空中。

sentences.en: I mean, that's astonishing.
sentences.zh: 我的天，这太惊人了。

sentences.en: That suggests that there is a kind of crisis-level frequency of planes nearly colliding.
sentences.zh: 这表明飞机差点相撞的频率已经达到了危机级别。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It was shocking.
sentences.zh: 这太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: It also confirmed what a lot of people involved in the industry were telling us, that this is happening just way, way more than the public realizes.
sentences.zh: 这也证实了许多业内人士对我们所说的话，这种情况发生的频率远超公众的认知。

sentences.en: Sadie, I want us to define this term we're using, because it's going to be very important for the rest of our conversation.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，我想让我们定义一下我们正在使用的这个词，因为这对于我们接下来的对话非常重要。

sentences.en: When we say close call, what exactly do we mean?
sentences.zh: 当我们说“险情”时，准确的含义是什么？

sentences.en: So a classic example is something that occurs on a runway where you can actually see it, where two planes get too close together, a pilot has to slam on the brakes.
sentences.zh: 一个典型的例子是发生在跑道上的那种你能亲眼看到的事故，两架飞机靠得太近，飞行员不得不猛踩刹车。

sentences.en: That's a classic example of a close call.
sentences.zh: 这是险情的一个典型例子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In the air, there are also rules about how close these planes can get to each other.
sentences.zh: 在空中，关于这些飞机之间可以靠得多近也有规定。

sentences.en: And in general, planes are not supposed to get within three miles horizontally and 1,000 feet vertically of each other.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，飞机之间水平距离不得小于三英里，垂直距离不得小于1,000英尺。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And this doesn't necessarily sound really close, especially if you're used to driving a car where these sound like pretty big distances.
sentences.zh: 这听起来不一定真的很近，特别是如果你习惯了开车，觉得这些听起来是不短的距离。

sentences.en: But remember that planes are going hundreds of miles an hour in the air, sometimes over 500 miles an hour, and these gaps can close within seconds.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，飞机在空中时速高达数百英里，有时甚至超过500英里，这些差距在几秒钟内就会缩短。

sentences.en: So, Sydney, give us some examples of the really close calls that you have been finding in these databases and in these FAA reports that most of us didn't even know have happened.
sentences.zh: 那么，悉尼，请给我们举几个你在这些数据库和美国联邦航空局报告中发现的真正惊险的例子，这些都是我们大多数人甚至不知道曾经发生过的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So in July, for example, there was an incident that occurred in New Orleans at the New Orleans
sentences.zh: 比如在7月份，新奥尔良发生了一起事故

sentences.en: Airport, where a Delta Airlines flight is preparing to take off on a runway, and at the same time, a Southwest plane is cleared to land on the exact same runway.
sentences.zh: 机场，一架达美航空公司的航班正准备在一条跑道上起飞，与此同时，一架西南航空公司的飞机获准在同一条跑道上降落。

sentences.en: The Southwest pilot realizes that it's getting too close and at the last second pulls up and aborts the landing and avoids a potential collision by just seconds.
sentences.zh: 西南航空的飞行员意识到距离太近了，在最后一秒拉起飞机并中止降落，仅凭几秒钟避免了一场潜在的碰撞。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, that would have been absolutely awful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那绝对会是一场惨剧。

sentences.en: An accelerating plane on the same runway as a very fast approaching landing plane would have potentially been catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 一架正在加速的飞机与一架极速迫近的降落飞机在同一跑道上，可能会造成灾难性的后果。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: And then a little over a week later in San Francisco, an American Airlines plane is accelerating down
sentences.zh: 就在一周多一点后，在旧金山，一架美国航空公司的飞机在跑道上加速起飞，时速超过160英里，险些撞上一架前沿航空公司的飞机，后者的机头已经探入了前者的跑道。

sentences.en: the runway for takeoff at more than 160 miles per hour and narrowly misses a Frontier Airlines plane whose nose had jutted into its path on the same runway.
sentences.zh: 就在一架前沿航空公司的飞机同一跑道上探出头来。

sentences.en: And then moments later, a German airliner is also accelerating for takeoff and just misses the Frontier Airlines plane.
sentences.zh: 紧接着，一架德国客机也在加速起飞，与前沿航空公司的飞机擦肩而过。

sentences.en: And so the American Airlines plane and the German airliner got so close to the Frontier Airlines
sentences.zh: 因此，美国航空公司的飞机和德国客机与前沿航空公司的飞机靠得如此之近，以至于在内部文件中，美国联邦航空局将这些遭遇描述为“机身贴机身”。

sentences.en: plane that in internal documents, the FAA describes these encounters as, quote, skin to skin.
sentences.zh: “机身贴机身”。

sentences.en: Which is a very evocative phrase.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常形象的词。

sentences.en: It sounds like a FAA way of saying way too close.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是美国联邦航空局用来形容“靠得太近了”的一种说法。

sentences.en: Way, way, way too close.
sentences.zh: 太近、太近、太近了。

sentences.en: And then two and a half weeks later in the sky, an American flight to Dallas was traveling
sentences.zh: 两周半后的空中，一架飞往达拉斯的美国航班正以

sentences.en: at more than 500 miles per hour when a collision alert blares in the cockpit because a United
sentences.zh: 超过500英里每小时的速度飞行，这时驾驶舱内警报声大作，因为一架联合航空公司的航班收到了错误的指令，正与这架美国航班处于相撞的航线上。

sentences.en: flight had been given incorrect instructions and was on a collision course with the American flight.
sentences.zh: 联合航空公司

sentences.en: At the last second, the American pilot had to yank the plane up and it climbed 700 feet to avoid a potential collision.
sentences.zh: 在最后一秒，美国航空的飞行员不得不猛拉飞机向上爬升了700英尺，以避免潜在的碰撞。

sentences.en: Sidney, these are clearly close calls, terrifyingly close calls, but none of them produced actual collisions.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，这些显然都是险情，极其惊险的险情，但它们都没有造成真正的碰撞。

sentences.en: And if you fly in America, you are constantly reminded that our passenger airline system is the safest in the world and planes don't crash.
sentences.zh: 如果你在美国坐飞机，你经常会被提醒，我们的客运航空系统是世界上最安全的，飞机不会坠毁。

sentences.en: They don't fall out of the sky.
sentences.zh: 它们不会从天上掉下来。

sentences.en: And so how worried should we really be about these close calls that you're describing?
sentences.zh: 所以，对于你所描述的这些险情，我们到底该有多担心？

sentences.en: So let's be clear.
sentences.zh: 让我们明确一点。

sentences.en: It is incredibly safe to fly.
sentences.zh: 坐飞机是非常安全的。

sentences.en: The last fatal crash involving a major U.S.
sentences.zh: 上一次涉及美国主流航空公司的致命坠机事故

sentences.en: airline occurred 14 years ago in 2009.
sentences.zh: 发生在14年前的2009年。

sentences.en: But what people are telling us is that that safety record sort of masks these risks that we've uncovered.
sentences.zh: 但人们告诉我们的是，那种安全记录在某种程度上掩盖了我们所发现的这些风险。

sentences.en: These near collisions are occurring so frequently that we have people in the aviation industry
sentences.zh: 这些差点相撞的事件发生得如此频繁，以至于航空业的人士

sentences.en: warning that we might be on borrowed time here, that a collision is more likely than you want to believe it is.
sentences.zh: 发出警告，称我们可能是在借时间过活，碰撞发生的可能性比你愿意相信的要大。

sentences.en: And so, for example, in the NASA database, there are some entries from pilots, and I'll read a couple of them if that's OK.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，在美国宇航局的数据库中，有一些来自飞行员的记录，如果不介意的话，我来读几个。

sentences.en: So in one, a longtime airline captain who'd been involved in a close call wrote, honestly, this stuff scares the crap out of me.
sentences.zh: 其中一个有丰富经验的航空公司机长在经历了一次险情后写道：“老实说，这把我吓得够呛。”

sentences.en: And another pilot, after being involved in a close call on a runway in January, wrote, this has really opened my eyes to how the next aviation accident may play out.
sentences.zh: 另一名飞行员在1月份经历了一次跑道险情后写道：“这真的让我大开眼界，看到了下一次空难可能会如何上演。”

sentences.en: And these kind of warnings are coming even from federal officials.
sentences.zh: 这类警告甚至来自联邦官员。

sentences.en: So in March, the chairwoman of the National Transportation Safety Board, she said, quote, the absence of a fatality or an accident doesn't mean the presence of safety.
sentences.zh: 因此在3月份，国家运输安全委员会的主席表示：“没有发生人员伤亡或事故并不等于具备安全。”

sentences.en: And she went on to say that these close calls must serve as a wake-up call for every single one of us before something more catastrophic occurs, before lives are loSt.
sentences.zh: 她接着说，这些险情必须成为我们每个人的警钟，在发生更具灾难性的事情、在生命逝去之前。

sentences.en: So, Sydney, the inevitable question is, why is this happening?
sentences.zh: 那么，悉尼，不可避免的问题是，为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Why are there so many close calls occurring on the ground and in the sky?
sentences.zh: 为什么地面和空中会发生这么多险情？

sentences.en: That's exactly the question we were asking people in the aviation industry.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们在航空业向大家提出的问题。

sentences.en: And what they told us was, this is emblematic of a safety system that is under incredible strain.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们的是，这象征着一个承受着巨大压力的安全系统。

sentences.en: And this safety system has been under strain for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而这个安全系统已经承受压力很长时间了。

sentences.en: But as air traffic starts returning to pre-pandemic levels, as everyone wants to fly, this is reaching a breaking point.
sentences.zh: 但随着空中交通开始恢复到大流行前的水平，随着每个人都想坐飞机，这已经达到了一个临界点。

sentences.en: The safety system is now so strained that it's reached a full-blown crisis.
sentences.zh: 安全系统现在承受的压力如此之大，以至于已经演变成了一场全面的危机。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温纳露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的一个字谜。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天都创作“拼字蜜蜂”和“字谜”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色彩联觉的病症。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: Sydney, tell us about this safety system that is clearly under some real strain.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，跟我们讲讲这个显然承受着巨大压力的安全系统吧。

sentences.en: So the safety system that keeps planes and passengers safe is really interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，保障飞机和乘客安全的这个安全系统真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: It's built on layers.
sentences.zh: 它是层层叠加构建的。

sentences.en: And you can think of these layers as there's the air traffic control layer, the people who are guiding the planes through the skies and into and out of airports.
sentences.zh: 你可以把这些层想象成：有空中交通管制层，也就是引导飞机穿过天空、进出机场的人员。

sentences.en: There are the pilots who are steering these planes and looking out at the skies around them.
sentences.zh: 有驾驶这些飞机并观察周围天空的飞行员。

sentences.en: And then you also have technology, technology on runways and technology on the planes themselves that alert controllers and pilots to potential collisions.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有技术，跑道上的技术以及飞机本身的技术，它们会向管制员和飞行员发出潜在相撞的警报。

sentences.en: And in aviation circles, the safety system is known as the Swiss cheese model.
sentences.zh: 在航空界，这个安全系统被称为“瑞士奶酪模型”。

sentences.en: So think about getting, you know, half a pound of Swiss cheese for your sandwiches at the grocery store and you have all these different slices.
sentences.zh: 你可以这样想，你在杂货店买了一磅切片瑞士奶酪做三明治，你有很多不同的切片。

sentences.en: If something slips through the hole on one slice, the odds are that the next slice underneath
sentences.zh: 如果有什么东西从一块奶酪的洞里滑过去，很有可能在下面紧接着的那一块

sentences.en: it, the holes are not going to align and the cheese is going to stop the thing from slipping through the rest of the stack of Swiss cheese.
sentences.zh: 奶酪上，这些洞是不会对齐的，奶酪会阻止这个东西从整叠瑞士奶酪的其余部分滑过去。

sentences.en: And there are all these redundancies built into the system.
sentences.zh: 而且系统中内置了所有这些冗余机制。

sentences.en: So if one layer fails, the other layers are going to catch it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果某一层失效了，其他层会接住它。

sentences.en: So based on your reporting, which of these layers is faltering and leading to these close calls?
sentences.zh: 那么根据你们的报道，这些层中哪一层正在动摇并导致了这些险情？

sentences.en: So what we found in our reporting was a lot of these close calls are caused by mistakes among air traffic controllers and also among pilots.
sentences.zh: 我们在报道中发现的是，许多险情都是由空中交通管制员以及飞行员的失误引起的。

sentences.en: And what we found was actually the most acute challenge is the shortage of air traffic controllers across the country.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，实际上最严峻的挑战是全国范围内空中交通管制员的短缺。

sentences.en: OK, so explain that.
sentences.zh: 好的，请解释一下。

sentences.en: Why is there a shortage of air traffic controllers and how is that leading to this problem of ghost calls?
sentences.zh: 为什么会短缺空中交通管制员？这又是如何导致这种虚惊事件的问题的？

sentences.en: So the shortage in air traffic controllers has been going on for years and it actually dates back to the early 1980s.
sentences.zh: 空中交通管制员的短缺已经持续多年，实际上可以追溯到20世纪80年代初。

sentences.en: Air traffic controllers went on strike illegally.
sentences.zh: 当时空中交通管制员举行了非法的罢工。

sentences.en: They're federal employees.
sentences.zh: 他们是联邦雇员。

sentences.en: They were not supposed to strike.
sentences.zh: 他们本不应该罢工。

sentences.en: And President Reagan fired them.
sentences.zh: 里根总统把他们都解雇了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He fired thousands of them.
sentences.zh: 他解雇了数千名管制员。

sentences.en: And to replenish the ranks, the government then had to hire new air traffic controllers.
sentences.zh: 为了补充人员队伍，政府随后不得不招聘新的空中交通管制员。

sentences.en: And what this did was it sort of knocked off kilter the natural cycle of hiring people and having those people eventually retire at different times.
sentences.zh: 这样做带来的结果是，它打破了招聘人员以及让这些人最终在不同时间退休的自然周期。

sentences.en: Instead, what you had was all of these controllers were hired at once and then it created mass waves of retirement.
sentences.zh: 相反，你遇到的是所有这些管制员都是同时被招聘的，这随后造成了一波又一波的大规模退休潮。

sentences.en: It gets a little it gets a little complicated, but air traffic controllers have to retire by the age of 56 and they start becoming eligible to retire after 20 years of service.
sentences.zh: 这有点，这有点复杂，但空中交通管制员必须在56岁前退休，他们在工作满20年后就开始具备退休资格。

sentences.en: And what happened was the FAA really just couldn't keep up with these mass retirements.
sentences.zh: 实际情况是，美国联邦航空局（FAA）实在无法跟上这些大规模的退休潮。

sentences.en: It started falling behind and then the pandemic hit and the pandemic made things just a lot worse.
sentences.zh: 它开始落后，接着大流行爆发了，大流行让情况变得更加糟糕。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: So, of course, you had air traffic controllers who quit or retired early, as happened around the country in lots and lots of different industries.
sentences.zh: 当然，你有一些空中交通管制员辞职或提前退休，就像全国各地许许多多不同的行业里发生的那样。

sentences.en: But it also slowed training.
sentences.zh: 但它也减缓了培训。

sentences.en: Training for air traffic controllers takes a while.
sentences.zh: 空中交通管制员的培训需要一段时间。

sentences.en: It's very intense.
sentences.zh: 非常紧张繁重。

sentences.en: But because of health restrictions, you couldn't train as many air traffic controllers as the
sentences.zh: 但由于健康限制，你无法培训像

sentences.en: FAA had to train.
sentences.zh: 美国联邦航空局原本需要培训的那么多空中交通管制员。

sentences.en: And so you just start falling more and more and more behind.
sentences.zh: 于是你就开始越来越落后。

sentences.en: And at this point, there are something like 10 percent fewer fully certified air traffic controllers than there were a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 到了现在，完全获得认证的空中交通管制员数量比十年前减少了大约10%。

sentences.en: In fact, we analyzed some numbers and there are only three air traffic facilities in the country that are considered fully staffed as of May.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们分析了一些数据，截至5月，全国只有三个航空交通设施被认为人员配备齐全。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Out of 313.
sentences.zh: 在313个设施中只有三个。

sentences.en: Sidney, the FAA presumably has had years to recognize this shortage as a natural extension of what Ronald Reagan did and to find ways to recruit to balance it out.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，美国联邦航空局按理说有多年时间来认识到这种短缺是罗纳德·里根所作所为的自然延伸，并寻找招募人员以平衡它的方法。

sentences.en: So why hasn't that happened?
sentences.zh: 那为什么没有发生呢？

sentences.en: Well, so the truth is that being a controller is a really, really demanding, difficult job.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实是，做一名管制员是一份非常、非常严苛、困难的工作。

sentences.en: It's highly stressful.
sentences.zh: 压力极大。

sentences.en: They are spending long, long hours staring at planes.
sentences.zh: 他们要花很长时间盯着飞机。

sentences.en: Think about trying to keep planes apart that you know have passengers on them.
sentences.zh: 想想看，试着把你知道载有乘客的飞机隔开。

sentences.en: And many controllers work a grueling schedule called the Rattler, which is essentially rotating
sentences.zh: 许多管制员实行一种名为“响尾蛇”（The Rattler）的折磨人的排班表，这基本上是轮班制，

sentences.en: shifts that start earlier and earlier in the day until you get to the last day of your schedule where you work two shifts in a 24-hour period.
sentences.zh: 一天比一天更早开始上班，直到排班的最后一天，你需要在24小时内上两个班。

sentences.en: This really messes with their sleep schedules.
sentences.zh: 这严重扰乱了他们的睡眠规律。

sentences.en: And if you don't have enough air traffic controllers, what ends up happening is many have to work mandatory six-day work weeks.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有足够的空中交通管制员，最终发生的情况就是许多人不得不进行强制性的每周六天工作制。

sentences.en: They have to work an extra day.
sentences.zh: 他们必须多上一天班。

sentences.en: And this is what they say is leading to a lot of these close calls.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们所说的导致许多此类险情的原因。

sentences.en: They're just so, so exhausted mentally, physically, that they can't focus and that the focus required to be an air traffic controller, they're just unable to keep for that long.
sentences.zh: 他们在精神上和身体上都太累、太累了，以至于无法集中精力，而作为空中交通管制员所必需的注意力，他们根本无法维持那么长时间。

sentences.en: So what about the pilots?
sentences.zh: 那么飞行员呢？

sentences.en: Why are they, as a layer of safety in the system, under strain right now when it comes to close calls?
sentences.zh: 作为系统中安全的一环，为什么他们在发生险情时目前也承受着压力？

sentences.en: So during the pandemic, you might remember that air traffic tanked.
sentences.zh: 在大流行期间，你可能还记得航空客运量暴跌。

sentences.en: No one wanted to fly on planes.
sentences.zh: 没有人想坐飞机。

sentences.en: And airlines started furloughing their pilots and encouraging their older pilots to retire.
sentences.zh: 航空公司开始让飞行员停薪留职，并鼓励年长的飞行员退休。

sentences.en: And what happened was these older, experienced pilots, a lot of them did retire.
sentences.zh: 结果是，这些年长、有经验的飞行员，很多人确实退休了。

sentences.en: And to replenish those ranks, the major carriers started drying on regional airline pilots.
sentences.zh: 为了补充这些人员，主要航空公司开始从支线航空公司的飞行员中抽调人手。

sentences.en: And the experience level in the cockpit decreased.
sentences.zh: 驾驶舱内的经验水平下降了。

sentences.en: So if you think about a 16-year-old driver versus a 45-year-old driver, the 16-year-old driver is going to be more prone to making mistakes.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想想一个16岁的司机和一个45岁的司机，16岁的司机更容易犯错。

sentences.en: This is what people in the industry tell us, that on average, the experience level of pilots is a little lower.
sentences.zh: 行业内的人士就是这样对我们说的，平均而言，飞行员的经验水平稍微低了一些。

sentences.en: They're a little less seasoned.
sentences.zh: 他们稍微没有那么老练。

sentences.en: So they're just more prone to making mistakes.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是更容易犯错。

sentences.en: But according to the Swiss cheese safety model, if I'm understanding what you told me correctly,
sentences.zh: 但根据瑞士奶酪安全模型，如果我没有理解错你刚才告诉我的话，

sentences.en: Sydney, an inexperienced pilot shouldn't be a huge problem if they make an error because the next layer is supposed to catch them.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，经验不足的飞行员如果犯了错，应该不会成为一个大问题，因为下一层应该能接住他们。

sentences.en: You know, the air traffic controller.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也就是空中交通管制员。

sentences.en: And even if that air traffic controller is overstretched or tired, they should have their error
sentences.zh: 而且即使那个空中交通管制员过度劳累或疲惫，他们的错误也应该

sentences.en: caught by a pilot, even if they are a little bit less experienced than in the past, right?
sentences.zh: 被飞行员发现并纠正，即使飞行员比过去稍微缺乏经验一点，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, that's the thinking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大家的设想是这样的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But what you can see is if you have less seasoned pilots in the cockpit and you have overworked, exhausted controllers, those holes in each layer of the Swiss cheese are
sentences.zh: 但你可以看到，如果驾驶舱里有经验较少的飞行员，同时又有过度劳累、精疲力竭的管制员，瑞士奶酪每一层的那些洞

sentences.en: getting bigger and they're more likely to align.
sentences.zh: 就会变大，并且它们更有可能对齐。

sentences.en: The mistake is going to slip through both layers.
sentences.zh: 错误就会从这两层中溜过去。

sentences.en: Take a recent incident in Phoenix that occurred in early AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 以8月初发生在菲尼克斯的最近一起事件为例。

sentences.en: A controller gave an instruction to a pilot on an American Airlines plane about the departure route he was supposed to take after he took off from the runway.
sentences.zh: 一名管制员向一架美国航空公司飞机的飞行员发出了指令，关于他从跑道起飞后应该采用的离场航线。

sentences.en: And the pilot repeated the instructions back incorrectly.
sentences.zh: 而飞行员错误地复述了这些指令。

sentences.en: The air traffic controller didn't hear the incorrect readback.
sentences.zh: 空中交通管制员没有听出错误的复述。

sentences.en: And so the American plane takes off.
sentences.zh: 于是这架美国航空公司的飞机起飞了。

sentences.en: And instead of turning right, it turns left.
sentences.zh: 它没有向右转，而是向左转了。

sentences.en: At the same time, a Southwest plane had taken off.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，一架西南航空公司的飞机已经起飞了。

sentences.en: And so this American plane is now turning into the path of the Southwest plane.
sentences.zh: 因此，这架美国航空公司的飞机现在正转向西南航空公司的飞行路径上。

sentences.en: American 1388 Phoenix departure.
sentences.zh: 美国航空1388，菲尼克斯离场。

sentences.en: Verify 4P1 departure.
sentences.zh: 请核实4P1离场程序。

sentences.en: We actually have the audio of when another controller realizes what's happening.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上拥有另一名管制员意识到发生情况时的录音。

sentences.en: 1388 traffic alert.
sentences.zh: 1388，交通警报。

sentences.en: It can sound kind of confusing.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能有点混乱。

sentences.en: The controller is repeating things to the pilot.
sentences.zh: 管制员在向飞行员重复事情。

sentences.en: The pilots are repeating it back.
sentences.zh: 飞行员在复述。

sentences.en: I'm sitting right there.
sentences.zh: 我就坐在那儿。

sentences.en: Do you see the traffic?
sentences.zh: 你看到那架飞机了吗？

sentences.en: 3P1, market 1388.
But what you really note is the urgency in the controller's voice.
sentences.zh: 但你真正注意到的是管制员声音中的紧迫感。

sentences.en: If you need to turn left, immediately do so.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要向左转，立刻照做。

sentences.en: He tells the Southwest plane, turn if you need to.
sentences.zh: 他告诉西南航空公司的飞机：如果需要的话就转弯。

sentences.en: Okay, did you make the turn?
sentences.zh: 好的，你转弯了吗？

sentences.en: We checked about 30 to the left.
sentences.zh: 我们向左盘旋了大约30度。

sentences.en: And eventually...
sentences.zh: 最终……

sentences.en: Turn.
sentences.zh: 转弯。

sentences.en: I'll make sure American turns out of your way here.
sentences.zh: 我会确保美国航空转开，不挡你的路。

sentences.en: The planes do start diverging.
sentences.zh: 这两架飞机确实开始分道扬镳了。

sentences.en: They do turn away from each other.
sentences.zh: 它们确实彼此转开了。

sentences.en: And the original sin in this situation is kind of a worst-case scenario for this multilayered system because you have an error by a pilot not being caught by that first controller.
sentences.zh: 而这种情况下的“原罪”对这个多层系统来说可以说是最糟糕的情况，因为飞行员犯下的错误没有被第一位管制员发现。

sentences.en: A kind of double failure.
sentences.zh: 一种双重失误。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And what happened was these planes got so close together, they got a third of a mile horizontally and 300 feet vertically to each other,
sentences.zh: 结果是，这两架飞机靠得如此之近，它们之间的水平距离只有三分之一英里，垂直距离只有300英尺，

sentences.en: which, with planes going hundreds of miles per hour, is so, so dangerously close.
sentences.zh: 考虑到飞机以每小时数百英里的速度飞行，这是非常、非常危险的近距离。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So then, Sydney, we get to the next layer of this safety system, what you call the technology that is supposed to keep these planes apart.
sentences.zh: 那么，悉尼，我们来到了这个安全系统的下一层，也就是你所说的本应让这些飞机保持距离的技术。

sentences.en: What's the story there, and why is it potentially contributing to the close calls?
sentences.zh: 那里的情况是怎样的？为什么它可能促成了这些险情？

sentences.en: So, most importantly, there is technology that alerts air traffic controllers to potential collisions.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，有一种技术可以向空中交通管制员发出潜在相撞的警报。

sentences.en: This is surface detection technology.
sentences.zh: 这就是地面探测技术。

sentences.en: But the problem there is that it's only at 43 airports in the country out of roughly 500 that serve commercial airlines.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，全国大约500个服务于商业航空公司的机场中，只有43个机场配备了这项技术。

sentences.en: Why so few?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么少？

sentences.en: So, it's very expensive to install, millions of dollars, and it's also old.
sentences.zh: 因为安装费用非常昂贵，要数百万美元，而且它也很老旧。

sentences.en: And the FAA says they're looking for newer technology.
sentences.zh: 美国联邦航空局表示他们正在寻找更新的技术。

sentences.en: But the result of not having this technology at so many airports is close calls around runways.
sentences.zh: 但在这么多机场没有这种技术的结果就是跑道附近的险情。

sentences.en: And you can see this, for instance, in Austin, in the example that I mentioned earlier involving the FedEx and Southwest planes that got really close to each other.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可以在奥斯汀看到这一点，在我之前提到的那个涉及联邦快递和西南航空飞机的例子中，这两架飞机靠得非常近。

sentences.en: Austin doesn't have this service technology.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀没有这项地面技术。

sentences.en: And that, people say, is one of the reasons these planes did get so close to each other before the FedEx pilot pulled up and avoided a collision.
sentences.zh: 人们说，这就是在联邦快递飞行员拉起飞机并避免相撞之前，这两架飞机靠得如此之近的原因之一。

sentences.en: And then there's another piece of technology that is really, really important on commercial airlines.
sentences.zh: 然后还有另一项技术，对商业航空公司来说非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: This technology is basically a collision avoidance technology.
sentences.zh: 这项技术基本上是一种防撞技术。

sentences.en: If two planes are getting too close to each other or are looking like they're going to get too close to each other,
sentences.zh: 如果两架飞机靠得太近，或者看起来将要靠得太近，

sentences.en: this technology blares in the cockpit and either alerts the pilot to potential traffic or tells the pilot to climb or descend if the planes are getting too close to each other.
sentences.zh: 这项技术就会在驾驶舱内发出巨响，要么向飞行员发出潜在交通警报，要么在飞机靠得太近时告诉飞行员爬升或下降。

sentences.en: So, Sydney, what is and what can be done to address all these strains?
sentences.zh: 那么，悉尼，有什么以及可以做些什么来解决所有这些压力？

sentences.en: Because everything you've told us suggests that the FAA knows about all these close calls.
sentences.zh: 因为你告诉我们的所有情况都表明，美国联邦航空局知道所有这些险情。

sentences.en: So why haven't they done more to try to prevent them?
sentences.zh: 那为什么他们没有做更多努力来试图阻止它们呢？

sentences.en: Well, it really comes down to money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这 realmente 归结为资金问题。

sentences.en: They would love to be able to hire more controllers, but it costs money.
sentences.zh: 他们很乐意能够雇用更多管制员，但这需要花钱。

sentences.en: They want to be able to install more technology on runways, but that also costs money.
sentences.zh: 他们希望能够在跑道上安装更多技术设备，但这同样需要花钱。

sentences.en: And they submit budget requests to Congress every year.
sentences.zh: 他们每年都会向国会提交预算申请。

sentences.en: But in the end, it's the money that they get.
sentences.zh: 但最终，这就是他们能得到的资金。

sentences.en: This is what they would tell us.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们会告诉我们的。

sentences.en: But even with these measures that they are saying they want to take, people tell us that this is just not enough.
sentences.zh: 但即使采取了他们声称想要采取的这些措施，人们告诉我们这依然远远不够。

sentences.en: The shortage in air traffic controllers is so severe that the number of air traffic controllers that the FAA wants to hire
sentences.zh: 空中交通管制员的短缺如此严重，以至于美国联邦航空局想要用他们现有的资金雇用的管制员数量

sentences.en: with the money that they have is not going to solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 根本无法解决这个问题。

sentences.en: The technology on runways is old and they need to find new technology.
sentences.zh: 跑道上的技术已经老旧，他们需要寻找新技术。

sentences.en: They say that they are working on that, but that could be years from being installed.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们正在为此努力，但这可能需要数年时间才能安装完毕。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of frustration right now among pilots and among air traffic controllers that they want attention on this.
sentences.zh: 所以目前飞行员和空中交通管制员当中有很多挫败感，他们希望外界关注这一点。

sentences.en: They want the public to know that close calls are happening and they want the FAA to do more.
sentences.zh: 他们希望公众知道险情正在发生，并希望美国联邦航空局做更多的工作。

sentences.en: Which makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这很合乎情理。

sentences.en: And Sydney, what's so interesting and important about the investigation that you and Emily Steele did is that it's coming before a deadly tragedy.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，你和艾米莉·斯蒂尔（Emily Steele）所做的调查之所以如此有趣且重要，是因为它出现在一场致命悲剧发生之前。

sentences.en: So often in journalism, we do this kind of reporting after something terrible happens.
sentences.zh: 在新闻界，我们经常在可怕的事情发生之后才做这种报道。

sentences.en: And here, you're finding that people are trying to ring the alarms and are ringing the alarms before and in anticipation of a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，你们发现人们正试图在悲剧发生前以及预见到悲剧时敲响警钟。

sentences.en: Which means that there is really an opportunity to prevent something awful from happening.
sentences.zh: 这意味着确实有机会阻止可怕事情的发生。

sentences.en: Yeah, there is an opportunity here.
sentences.zh: 是的，这里确实有一个机会。

sentences.en: But what a lot of people we talked to said was they are worried that nothing is going to happen or that the FAA is not going to do enough.
sentences.zh: 但我们采访的很多人都说，他们担心什么都不会改变，或者美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）做的事情不够。

sentences.en: There is this sort of very, very cynical take, which is that the FAA in some circles is known as the tombstone agency.
sentences.zh: 有一种非常非常愤世嫉俗的观点，认为FAA在某些圈子里被称为“墓碑机构”。

sentences.en: That is, they won't do anything until something catastrophic does occur, until people do die.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在发生灾难性事件、人员伤亡之前，他们什么都不会做。

sentences.en: The people we talk to say there really is no excuse for the FAA not to do something before one of these close calls leads to a fatal crash.
sentences.zh: 我们采访的人表示，在这些险情导致致命坠机事件发生之前，FAA没有理由不采取行动。

sentences.en: Sydney, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们不胜感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Monday, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky pushed out his defense minister, the biggest shakeup in the leadership of Ukraine's war effort
sentences.zh: 周一，乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基撤换了他的国防部长，这是自去年俄罗斯入侵该国以来，

sentences.en: since Russia invaded the country last year.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰战时领导层最大的一次改组。

sentences.en: The move is significant because the defense minister,
sentences.zh: 此举意义重大，因为这位国防部长

sentences.en: Alexei Reznikov, has been a close advisor to Zelensky and a public face of Ukraine's battle against Russia.
sentences.zh: 阿列克谢·列兹尼科夫一直是泽连斯基的亲密顾问，也是乌克兰抗击俄罗斯的公众形象代表。

sentences.en: Zelensky did not specify why he was replacing Reznikov, but the decision comes amid widening corruption investigations
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基没有说明他为什么要撤换列兹尼科夫，但这一决定正值针对

sentences.en: into the mishandling of military contracts related to the war.
sentences.zh: 与战争相关的军事合同管理不善的腐败调查不断扩大之际。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，美国

sentences.en: revealed that the leader of North Korea, Kim Jong-un, plans to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss the possibility of supplying Russia
sentences.zh: 透露，朝鲜领导人金正恩计划与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京会面，讨论向俄罗斯提供

sentences.en: with more weaponry for its war against Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 更多武器以用于对乌战争的可能性。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: hopes that by exposing such an arrangement, it will discourage North Korea from following through with an arms deal to Russia, a strategy that has worked in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 希望通过曝光这样一项安排，能够阻止朝鲜最终与俄罗斯达成武器交易，这一策略过去曾奏效过。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由亚历克斯·斯特恩制作，

sentences.en: Stella Tan, Rob Zipko, and Shannon Lynn.
sentences.zh: 斯特拉·谭、罗布·齐普科和香农·林恩。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lexi Dio, contains original music by Marian Lozano and Dan Powell, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 节目由莱西·迪奥剪辑，包含马里安·洛萨诺和丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐，由阿莉莎·莫克斯利担任音频工程。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landverk of Wonderland.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由奇境乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰德维克创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱且有时令人激动的内斗中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《都市》最新一期节目中，由我萨拉·科尼格为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却一路失控的故事。
